subject: Integration: QuickConnect SDK + local validation plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Emily Grant <emily@lumina.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Integration: QuickConnect SDK + local validation plan

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for a great discovery call earlier. Per our convo I wanted to capture a concise integration plan so your infra and dev teams have a clear, testable path to validate Redwood in a local/sandbox environment. TL;DR: we can get you a working Python + TypeScript sample app that exercises auth, routing (regional pinning), structured output/tool-calling, and embeddings/reranker flows within 3 business days once we have the sandbox credentials listed below.

Summary of next steps (action items):
- Lumina: provide a sandbox API gateway URL (or sample VPC peering window) and a short-lived service account API key we can use for end-to-end tests. If you prefer IP allowlist, please share the CIDR blocks.
- Lumina: indicate whether requests must stay inside us-west region (latency sensitive) or if you can accept eu-central fallback.
- Redwood: share SDK quickstart bundle (Python/TS), two sample apps (chat + embedding-based search), and a minimal reranker evaluation script. Attachment: redwood_quickconnect_v1.pdf (quickstart) and sample-apps-readme.md.
- Joint: schedule a 60-min hands-on session (we recommend dev+infra) to run the local validation checklist and confirm metrics (p99 latency, tokens/sec, and embedding cosine similarity baseline).

Local validation checklist (dev-focused):
1) Install dependencies (Python 3.11, Node 18) and clone quickconnect-samples repo.
2) Configure SDK auth: either API key in environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY or optional IAM/OIDC exchange flow (we can provide a sample).
3) Run sample chat app (local port) with streaming enabled and verify tool-calling stub returns structured JSON.
4) Run embedding + reranker flow: ingest 1k docs, compute embeddings, run candidate generation + rerank, compare top-5 to known-good baseline.

Notes about architecture choices we discussed:
- Auth: API key is easiest for sandbox; for production you can plug your OIDC provider and we support token exchange flows.
- Routing: we expose a routing hint in the request header (X-Redwood-Region) so you can pin to us-west for low latency or let SmartRouting select cheaper fallback.
- Structured output & tools: we include a small tool-binding library in the TS SDK that helps map model JSON -> typed calls; sample in the repo demonstrates a DB lookup tool.

Attachments: redwood_quickconnect_v1.pdf, sample-apps-readme.md

Proposed times for the joint session: Tue 2027-08-17 10:00 PT or Wed 2027-08-18 09:00 PT. Let me know which works and who from your side will join.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Emily Grant <emily@lumina.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: QuickConnect SDK + local validation plan

Emily — thanks for the quick reply and the attendee list. Answers below to your clarifying questions + a compressed plan we can run during the 60-min session.

1) Reranker evaluation size: 1k documents is a fine minimum. For more robust signals run 5k-10k (overnight ingest); for the quick session we'll validate correctness with 500-1k and then run a 5k ingest as a follow-up. We'll provide a synthetic dataset generator in the repo.

2) Local vector DB: we recommend running Milvus or Pinecone local emulator for parity. The quickconnect-samples default uses SQLite + FAISS for a light reproducible baseline (fast to start). We'll include a Docker compose that spins up FAISS + local Redis cache.

3) Latency test harness: yes — the TS and Python SDKs include a small load-replay tool (scripts/load_replay.py and scripts/load_replay.ts) that will replay recorded sequences with configurable concurrency and record p50/p95/p99. We'll attach a short runbook in the repo.

60-min session runbook (45 mins hands-on + 15 mins review):
- 0-10m: environment check (node/python versions, REDWOOD_API_KEY present, network access).
- 10-25m: run chat sample with streaming + tool call; verify structured JSON output mapped to tool handler.
- 25-40m: run embedding ingest (500 docs) + candidate generation + rerank; check top-5 results and sample accuracy.
- 40-50m: run load_replay at low concurrency to capture baseline p50/p95/p99.
- 50-60m: next steps and production considerations (auth patterns for prod, routing policy choices, and observability knobs).

I attached a small spreadsheet with the test matrix (lumina-integration-matters.xlsx) to help you prepare. If Jay needs the CIDR list for allowlist, I can provide our short list of sandbox IPs.

Confirming: Tue 2027-08-17 10:00 PT works for us. I've tentatively booked time and will send an invite after you confirm Jay.

-Kim

Hi Emily / team —

A couple of practical notes from engineering:
- Sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickconnect-samples (already linked in the drive). The "samples/embedding-rerank" directory has the synthetic generator and a small Docker compose for FAISS + Redis.
- Auth examples: ~/.redwoodrc for API-key local testing; oidc/README.md for the exchange flow (we can demo this during the session).
- Structured output: the TypeScript SDK returns a strongly-typed object when you call client.tools.invoke("search_db", payload) — the sample shows JSON schema validation before invoking downstream handlers.

If you want I can drop a short (15-line) script to automate the 500-doc ingest and produce a comparison CSV of top-5 vs baseline. LMK and I'll attach it to the drive.

Looking forward to the session.

—Dev
